analysis.investment_thesis: Gland Pharma scores poorly on both Magic Formula pillars: earnings yield of ~4.6% (EV ~INR 27,371 Cr, EBIT INR 1,269 Cr) is well below the 6% minimum, and ROIC of ~17% is sub-par for a specialty pharma business. With net profit declining -2% CAGR over 5 years and ROE at a meager 7.81%, this is neither cheap nor good.
key_strengths: Near-zero leverage (D/E 0.03, net cash of ~INR 2,242 Cr) provides balance sheet safety
Strong gross margins of 58.9% reflect injectable formulation pricing power and B2B CDMO model
Revenue CAGR of 16.4% (2020→2025) shows top-line growth capacity in regulated markets (US, EU, Australia)
key_risks: Earnings yield ~4.6% (EBIT 1,269/EV 27,371) — deeply below Magic Formula's 6% floor; market is pricing in perfection that hasn't materialized
Net profit collapsed from INR 1,212 Cr (2022) to INR 699 Cr (2025) — a 42% peak decline with no recovery; EBITDA margins compressed while revenue grew, signalling structural cost issues
Fosun Pharma (Chinese conglomerate) controls 51.83% — elevated geopolitical and governance risk, with limited promoter accountability to minority shareholders
red_flags: ROE of 7.81% on a ~INR 9,562 Cr equity base is capital destruction territory — earning far below cost of equity
Finance costs surged from INR 7 Cr (2020) to INR 42 Cr (2025) — 43% CAGR, inconsistent with 'debt-free' narrative
Investing CF volatile (swings from -1,749 to +1,718 Cr) suggests large treasury/investment churn masking weak core business returns
ROCE of only 11.9% — barely above risk-free rate; the business is not earning excess returns on its enormous asset base
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula math kills the thesis quickly. Enterprise Value = Market Cap (29,613) + Debt (314) − Cash (2,556) = INR 27,371 Cr. EBIT (operating income) = INR 1,269 Cr. Earnings Yield = 4.6% — well below the 6% floor that triggers any interest, and a fraction of the 12%+ that signals genuine cheapness. Invested capital (Equity + Debt − Cash) = ~INR 7,320 Cr yields ROIC of ~17%, which is mediocre — decent for a capital-heavy manufacturer, but not the 25%+ moat-signalling ROIC I want to pair with a cheap price. The business is neither cheap nor exceptional; it sits in the worst quadrant of the Magic Formula matrix.

The operating story is equally troubled. Revenue grew 16.4% CAGR but net profit shrank -2% CAGR, meaning every rupee of incremental revenue came at deteriorating economics — operating leverage working in reverse. EBITDA grew only 7% vs revenue at 16%, confirming margin dilution. Free cash flow conversion is acceptable (INR 521 Cr FCF vs 699 Cr net profit) but OCF/Net Profit is declining. The Chinese parent's majority stake adds a non-trivial governance premium that further discounts intrinsic value. At P/E 34x on shrinking earnings, there is no margin of safety — the Magic Formula firmly signals AVOID.
